Rencontre avec Christelle, première jour: Meet Christelle, La Converse’s First Journalist
J’ai toujours adoré la lecture, et l’écr: I’ve always loved reading, and writing became a passion that has never gone away.
Depuis le mois de juin, Christelle fait: Since June, Christelle has been part of our team of contributing journalists. Many La Converse readers recognize her and congratulate her on her work. She has also agreed to let one of her articles be used in a doctoral course at Stanford University. Other universities have invited her to speak about the content of her articles in their faculties. Because of the way she approaches the news, Christelle doesn’t leave anyone indifferent. We sat down with La Converse’s first full-time journalist.
<strong>‍</strong>Je souhaite devenir jo: ‍I’ve wanted to be a journalist since I was very young. When I was 12, I read La Presse religiously every morning! I’ve always loved reading, and writing became a passion that has never gone away. Then, when it came time for university, I wasn’t accepted into journalism; I was on waiting lists several times. I studied in related fields – literature and translation. It was a time when journalism was changing a lot. La Presse was announcing that it was going digital. We were told not to go into journalism, that there would be no jobs. It was also the time when blogs were multiplying.
J’ai d’ailleurs eu la chance de contribu: I was lucky enough to contribute to several of them, notably covering the music and cultural scene. Music is my other passion: I’m a singer-songwriter and a harpist. After that, I mostly worked in communications and culture. For a long time I was happy being a journalist on the side, but the desire to make it my career never faded, even though I had to be realistic. Over time, I also started to understand the obstacles, including systemic ones, that I was facing professionally. More recently, the murders of George Floyd and Breonna Taylor awakened a sense of urgency in me.
Je me suis dit qu’il fallait que je suiv: I told myself I had to follow my dreams. It gave me a second wind and pushed me to seize the opportunity to redirect my career toward journalism. The desire to raise people’s awareness of racism also played an important role.
‍<strong>Quel est pour toi le rôle du jo: ‍What do you see as the role of a journalist?
<strong>‍</strong>C’est un titre que je: ‍It’s a title I’ve only recently managed to embrace; I’ve always been quick to call myself a writer, an author or a musician. There’s a weight and a responsibility that come with calling yourself a journalist; you’re perceived as an influential person, which I sometimes find difficult. But it’s a title I’m honoured to carry. Above all, I want to share stories and have them be heard. Right now, in the media landscape and on social media, we see a lot of journalists presenting their opinions and writing columns.
Je veux faire tout le contraire – ce qui: I want to do the exact opposite – which is also in line with La Converse’s editorial approach. As a person, I have an enormous number of opinions, but as a journalist, I want to help people express themselves. In the current context, I think the role of the journalist needs to be reexamined. We need to take a step back.
L’activisme est beaucoup mis en lumière: Activism has been getting a lot of attention lately, which is a good thing.
Par contre, il faut faire la distinction: But we have to distinguish between journalism and activism. Often, when a racialized person speaks up, they’re labelled an activist, sometimes in a pejorative way. As a journalist, my goal is to share information. That doesn’t mean I’m not an activist in my everyday life. But it’s not my profession. I really draw a sharp line between my job and who I am as a person.
‍<strong>Comment as-tu connu La Converse: ‍How did you find out about La Converse?
<strong>‍</strong>Par une amie journalis: ‍Through a journalist friend, Ruby Pratka, who writes for La Converse. She had approached me about an article, and I wanted to know more. I read a huge amount of news and reporting. When I discovered La Converse, I was struck: I had never seen anything like it. Only a few articles had been published, but the topics interested me, the reporting was in-depth, and the writing was good. I immediately wanted to work with them.
‍<strong>Qu’est ce qui te réjouit à l’id: ‍What excites you about joining La Converse?
<strong>‍</strong>J’ai été agréablement: ‍I was pleasantly surprised when I read La Converse’s 10 values: I didn’t know it was possible to do journalism with that kind of mission! I found the content of the articles unprecedented and refreshing. We constantly see cuts and closures in the media, and I believe the quality of journalism is suffering because of it. When I discovered La Converse, which was just starting out, I wanted a project like this to continue and grow. I saw myself in dialogue-based, community-based journalism. Those were concepts that were new to me, but they reflected well what I wanted to read and to do. I was drawn to the idea of conversation, of being at the service of people and communities. In life, I always want to be close to people, whether through writing or music.
‍<strong>La Converse est une nouvelle pl: ‍La Converse is a new platform. What do you want people to know about the work being done here?
<strong>‍</strong>On est à l’écoute. On: ‍We listen. We act in the public’s interest. We don’t show up with our own ideas; we go to people and let them tell us about their concerns. I think we truly have an inclusive approach.
‍<strong>Tu as déjà écrit plusieurs arti: ‍You’ve already written several articles for La Converse. What’s different compared to other media outlets? What do you work on first?
<strong>‍</strong>La première étape, c’e: ‍The first step is to observe and listen. Then it’s to go to people. We look at which voices are missing, and we talk to different stakeholders. In that sense, there isn’t really a set process. What’s distinctive is that the perspectives shift along the way, because it’s by talking with people that the angle takes shape and the story comes together. It’s really unique. It’s been a real learning experience, because it doesn’t match at all the way I was taught to work: the subject doesn’t come from me, but from the people living a situation.
<strong>Quelle est l’incidence de ton ex: How does your experience as a Black journalist affect your work?
<strong>‍</strong>C’est sûr que mon expé: ‍Of course my experience influences how I perceive things. I don’t necessarily have the same blind spots.
<strong>Comment vois-tu l’avenir de La C: How do you see the future of La Converse? What topics would you like to cover?
<strong>‍</strong>Je souhaite que les ge: ‍I want people to be able to see themselves in our reporting, and they’re the ones who will tell us if they do! I want to cover current events, but differently. I hope we keep up our momentum and, above all, grow. We’re a new media outlet, and I’d like us to establish ourselves further and take our place in the media space, while staying close to communities. I want the project to expand so we can cover even more topics and be even more on the ground. I think we’re off to a good start.
